title: Vide
pitch: An in-browser code-based video editor empowering AI agents to author timeline scripts, manage local media assets, and export MP4s via WebMCP.
about_excerpt: An in-browser code-based video editor empowering AI agents to author timeline scripts, manage local media assets, and export MP4s via WebMCP. Like Comment Story Updates Vide: In-browser Video IDE The 28 WebMCP Tools by Domain: Asset Metadata & Semantic Notes (3 tools): get_asset_metadata , set_asset_notes , search_assets — Attach and search semantic descriptions, mood tags, BPM tempos, spoken transcripts, and visual descriptions so the agent understands raw media files (e.g., matching "whoosh transition" to sfx_0294.mp3 ). File System Operations (4 tools): list_project_files , read_project_file , write_project_file , delete_project_file — Direct read/write access to project directory files and scripts. Script & Tab Lifecycle (8 tools): get_active_script , get_video_script , set_active_script_code , update_video_script , create_script , list_open_scripts , switch_active_script , save_active_script — Read, generate, and hot-reload DSL scripts with real-time agent reasoning banners. Engine & Playback Telemetry (3 tools): validate_script , get_scene_settings , control_playback — Perform dry-run syntax checks, inspect canvas dimensions/FPS, and drive timeline playback. Hardware Video Export (1 tool): export_video — Trigger client-side GPU video encoding with configurable codecs (H.264/AVC, AV1, VP9) and automatically save outputs to the project's export folder. Documentation & Knowledge Base (3 tools): search_vide_docs , search_vide_documentation , get_dsl_reference — Embedded vector-scored knowledge base for the agent to look up DSL syntax, math rendering, and composition rules on the fly. Multimodal Visual Inspection & QA (3 tools): capture_frame_screenshot , analyze_timeline , inspect_layers_at_time — Render in-memory frame buffers to base64 PNGs for multimodal vision models to visually verify text alignment, contrast, and layout, correcting bugs autonomously. Timeline Cues & Scene Navigation (3 tools): list_timeline_cues , seek_to_cue , add_timeline_cue — Manage timeline markers, gutter breakpoints, and playhead anchors across scenes. How We Built It Having no formal background in compiler design, AST manipulation, or custom DSLs prior to this project, I paired with ChatGPT and Gemini as collaborative engineering partners throughout development. We established that compiling a deterministic subset of JavaScript using Acorn was the ideal architecture—giving users familiar syntax with mathematical operators, while completely eliminating non-deterministic loops and security risks in the evaluation sandbox. Technical Stack: Framework & Routing: Full-stack local-first application built with TanStack Start , React 19, and Tailwind CSS v4. Agent Protocol: WebMCP Bridge exposing 28 structured tools over window.modelContext and message channels. Language Runtime: Acorn for AST parsing, evaluated in a deterministic sandbox with Valibot schema validation at every trust boundary. Code Editor: Monaco Editor with custom Monarch tokenizers, syntax highlighters, and DSL snippet completions. Engine & Export: Custom HTML5 Canvas 2D engine paired with Mediabunny for WebCodecs MP4/WebM hardware encoding and Web Audio API mixing. Storage & Hosting: IndexedDB with the File System Access API; deployed serverlessly on Cloudflare Workers . Challenges We Ran Into Deterministic Timeline Architecture: Translating declarative composition ( parallel , sequence , at , after , gap , offset ) into an immutable, time-addressable AST graph while preventing timeline keyframe collisions. Synchronizing Video, Audio, and Canvas Lifecycles: Ensuring Mediabunny's frame-exact video reader and the Web Audio context stayed strictly aligned during interactive timeline scrubbing and offline hardware encoding. Cross-Platform WebCodecs Audio Encoding: Overcoming platform-specific audio encoder limitations (such as Linux Chromium lacking AAC encoders) by implementing dynamic AudioEncoder.isConfigSupported fallback routing between AAC and Opus inside MP4 containers. Designing a Clean 28-Tool WebMCP Surface: Structuring a comprehensive tool suite that allows deep multimodal inspection without overwhelming the agent's context window. Accomplishments That We're Proud Of Zero-Server Video Encoding: Rendering 60 FPS 1080p MP4 videos with custom fonts and LaTeX math entirely within the client browser using WebCodecs and Mediabunny. Complete 28-Tool WebMCP Suite: Enabling multimodal AI models to discover assets, author scripts, visually inspect rendered frames, and export motion graphics autonomously. True Dogfooding: The entire demonstration and challenge submission video was 100% scripted, animated, composed, and rendered inside Vide itself. Local-First Privacy: Full file editing, local asset references, and MP4 generation without a single byte of user media ever leaving their machine. What We Learned How to design a clean Domain-Specific Language (DSL) and evaluate AST nodes deterministically. How to leverage the WebCodecs API and Mediabunny for client-side, hardware-accelerated video export pipelines. The transformative power of the WebMCP standard in replacing brittle visual UI scraping with structured, bidirectional tool interfaces between web applications and AI agents. What's Next for Vide Orama In-Browser Vector Database: Integrating Orama to provide client-side vector search and semantic similarity matching across asset transcriptions, visual descriptions, and DSL documentation with sub-millisecond local latency. Web Worker OffscreenCanvas Rendering: Offloading the entire frame rendering and WebCodecs encoding pipeline into background Web Workers for faster export throughput. Procedural Data Visualization Nodes: Built-in animated bar charts, line plots, and telemetry counter primitives. Smart Audio Ducking: Automatic volume ducking on music tracks when voiceover layers are active. Direct Canvas Transform Gizmos: Interactive handles to manipulate shapes on screen while two-way syncing coordinates directly back into the DSL code.
